title.narrative: Improving the Quality of Basic Education in the North Pacific

description.narrative: The proposed Improving Quality of Basic Education in the North Pacific Project will improve quality of basic education in the Federated States of Micronesia and the Republic of Marshall Islands. The project will improve student learning outcomes through a set of comprehensive and sustained initiatives over 6 years. The project will focus on developing the following output areas: (i) Better prepared teachers in primary education; (ii) Strengthened capacity to use assessment to improve learning (iii) Expanded access and usage of bilingual teaching and learning resources and materials (TLRM) for literacy and numeracy; and (iv) Strengthened governance and management of schools, including parent/community engagement.

Output: Access to and usage of teaching and learning resources and materials for literacy and numeracy expanded Indicator: 90% of teachers (of which 50% are female) have participated in professional learning on resource use to improve student learning by 2025 (2017 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: FSM: By 2025, 87% (184 female [55%] and 151 male [45%]) of project school teachers have participated in professional learning on resource use to improve student learning.
RMI: Achieved. Total of 181 teachers (126 female; 55 male). There are 181 elementary teachers in IQBE project schools and all have received training on resource use at least once. Teachers who have attended QPF workshops have been exposed to new and valuable resources created by the IQBE Specialists themselves. Qualitative teaching and learning are demonstrated through the activities and resources included in all QPF lesson plans. Data Source: Project reports, MOE/DOE records, observation tools. Actual value:

Output: Access to and usage of teaching and learning resources and materials for literacy and numeracy expanded Indicator: FSM & RMI: 75% of teachers (of which 50% are female) access resources via flash drive, online catalogue, or resource center using newly established process by 2025 Progress/Status: FSM: Achieved. By 2025, 87% (184 female [55%] and 151 male [45%]) of project school teachers demonstrated access to project resources via online catalogue or resource center using the process established.
RMI: Achieved. A total of 351 teachers (228 female, 123 male) have access to resources via flash drive, online catalogue, or resource center using newly established process. The goal is to provide access to resources for 135 teachers from all project islands. So far, 351 teachers combined from both IQBE and non-IQBE schools have received access to resources on flash drives or online. 255 teachers have access to flash drives with QPF lesson plans while 66 teachers have access to online Math and English 5-weekly lesson plans. Data Source: Project reports, MOE/DOE records, observation tools. Actual value:

Output: Capacity to use student assessment to improve learning strengthened Indicator: RMI: At least 250 teachers (of which 50% are female) participate in professional learning about using alternative assessments for learning (e.g., EGLA, SAL, SAM) by 2024. Progress/Status: Achieved: A total of 392 teachers across all project islands were trained on formative and summative assessment tools, exceeding our target of at least 250 teachers. Teachers are actively using SAL and SAM data to adjust lessons to better meet students' needs. A National Students Assessment Framework was completed in October 2025 and endorsed by the EC in November 2025. Data Source: Project reports, MOE/DOE records Actual value:

Output: Educational leadership and management of schools, including parent and community engagement strengthened Indicator: All school improvement plans include five activities or projects that engage parents and community by 2025 Progress/Status: FSM: By 2025, 82% (18/22) of project schools had drafted components of their school improvement plans that included indigenous learning recovery activities for parents, community, teachers and students.
RMI: Canoe curriculum project has been delivered on project and non-project islands. Data Source: Project reports, MOE/DOE records, observation tools. Actual value:

Output: Teachers in primary education are better prepared Indicator: FSM: 800 teachers trained in QPF to teach numeracy and literacy across the curriculum in the medium of instruction by 2023 (2017 baseline:100 male/female 40% of participating schools implemented a system of lead teachers and induction by 2025 (2017 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: Achieved. By 2025, 886 teachers [521 female (59%) and 365 male (41%)] were trained nationwide in QPF to teach literacy and numeracy.
Achieved. 100% of participating schools have implemented a system of lead teachers and induction. Data Source: New policy documents; project progress reports Actual value:

Output: Educational leadership and management of schools, including parent and community engagement strengthened Indicator: FSM & RMI: 90% of principals (of which 40% are female) participate in professional learning (2017 baseline: 15%; 70% male and 30% female) Progress/Status: FSM: Achieved. 100% (8 female [37%] and 14 male [63%]) of principals have participated in professional learning.
RMI: Achieved. 90% of principals have participated in professional learning. There are 25 school Principals and vice Principals in the IQBE project schools and all of them have received some sort of training over the years. 8 leaders currently in project schools were trained in the Graduate Certificate in School Leadership (GCSL). Overall, 67 Principals have been trained under the project. Data Source: Project reports, MOE/DOE records, observation tools. Actual value:

Data Source: DOE and MOE records; project progress reports. Actual value:

Output: Capacity to use student assessment to improve learning strengthened Indicator: FSM and RMI: New national student assessment for learning framework developed by 2024 and approved and implemented by 2025 50% of participating teachers (of which 50% are female) use student assessment data to tailor teaching practice to meet student learning needs by 2025 (2017 baseline: 140) Progress/Status: FSM: 2a: Achieved: A new national student assessment for learning framework was developed, approved and implemented by 2024.
2b: Exceeded: By 2025, 64% (99 of 155) of participating teachers (101 female [65%] and 54 male [35%]) used student assessment data to tailor their teaching practice to meet student learning needs. COM-FSM mentor professors assessed this through classroom observations conducted as part of the project's induction program.
RMI: A total of 392 teachers across all project islands were trained on formative and summative assessment tools, exceeding our target of at least 250 teachers. Teachers are actively using SAL and SAM data to adjust lessons to better meet students' needs. A National Students Assessment Framework was completed in October 2025 and endorsed by the EC in November 2025. Data Source: Project reports, MOE/DOE records Actual value:

Output: Teachers in primary education are better prepared Indicator: RMI and FSM: A national teaching professional learning framework is drafted by 2021 and approved and implemented by 2025 Progress/Status: FSM: Achieved. A national teaching professional learning framework was drafted in 2022, approved in 2023, and implemented in 2024. This includes both the National Professional Learning and Development Framework and the National Teacher Quality Standards.
RMI: The final version of the National Professional Learning Framework (NPLF) was submitted in October 2025 and endorsed by PSS' Executive Committee (EC) in November 2025.
